label: Chrysococcyx_klaas
summary: Klaas's cuckoo (Chrysococcyx klaas) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae which is native to the wooded regions of sub-Saharan Africa. The specific name honours Klaas, the Khoikhoi man who collected the type specimen.

appearance.description: Klaas's cuckoo is 16–18 cm (6.3–7.1 inches) in length. The species exhibits sexual dimorphism. Males have a glossy green body with few markings and plain white underparts.
appearance.colors: Males have a glossy green body with few markings and plain white underparts. Females have a bronze-brown body, greenish wing coverts and faintly barred white underparts.
appearance.wings: Females have a bronze-brown body, greenish wing coverts and faintly barred white underparts.

where_found.habitat: The species occurs throughout sub-Saharan Africa with the exception of very arid areas in the south-west.
